key_insight: Physics-aligned electronic ground-state models generalize much better than standard ML interatomic potentials by constraining learning to physically meaningful degrees of freedom.
engineering_relevance: This work offers a lower-cost alternative between MLIPs and KS-DFT for more reliable energy and force prediction in materials, molecular, and reactive chemistry workflows.
method: Add physical constraints to ground-state descriptor models to match KS-DFT structure and reduce unphysical optimization.
Use OrthoNormal-Loss (ON-Loss) plus GROOT for density GSMs, and ON-Loss plus ROCKET for Hamiltonian GSMs.
Apply self-consistency rejection and label-free fine-tuning to improve robustness and transferability.
evidence_signal: Across QM9→QM40 extrapolation, the proposed methods cut energy/force MAE substantially, and on QMugs they rejected fewer than 0.4% of predictions while reaching 0.07 mHa energy MAE.
watch_item: The approach relies on careful physical constraints and rejection/filtering, so performance may depend on model/gauge design and could be less straightforward to deploy without KS-DFT-aligned training data.
paper_title: Physics-Aligned Electronic Ground-State Learning Improves Generalization
